label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**AN OPEN LETTER FROM THANDI — please feel free to forward this on**

*(If you're only reading one bit, skip to the section in the middle with the link. That's the only place to send money, and there's a fake page going around that I need people to know about.)*

---

Hi everyone,

I know my phone has been going off since Saturday night and I haven't replied to most of you. I'm sorry. I've read every single message — many of you more than once — and I've cried at about half of them. I just don't have the words or the hands for one-by-one replies right now. So here's one letter that covers everything. Please pass it on to whoever you think needs it.

**The short version: I'm safe.** I'm alive, I'm at my sister's place in Rondebosch, I'm fed, I have a bed and a working kettle. Marmalade is also alive and currently sitting on my head as I type this. That's the headline.

**What happened**

The fire started at around 11:40pm on Saturday night, 7 November, in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road, Observatory. My flat is number 12, on the second floor, and it wasn't the one that caught fire — but the smoke and the water from the fire hoses did most of the damage. The ceiling came down in my lounge.

Everyone got out. All 14 flats, all of us. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and sent home the same night. The fire department are still investigating and their working theory is an electrical fault, but they're not saying that yet, so neither will I. I'm not going to guess and I'm not going to relive it in detail — I really don't want to.

How I woke up was my neighbour, Uncle Faizel, going door to door on our floor in his vest and his slippers, banging and shouting. I will never forget that sound. He didn't wait for me to answer, he just kept going, and that is the only reason I got out at all.

I grabbed my phone and Marmalade. Nothing else. No documents, no clothes, no laptop. Marmalade hid under my car for two hours afterwards and then came out like nothing had happened, which I choose to interpret as a personal insult.

The landlord says nobody goes back into the flats for at least six weeks. So my home is currently a smoke-and-water zone with a collapsed ceiling, and I'll be living somewhere else until at least mid-December.

**The sad bit, quickly**

The end-of-year concert stuff I'd taken home to laminate is gone. All 22 crowns and the children's handprint banner. I'm sad about it, but furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can't. So that's where my priorities are.

**The fundraiser — the only legitimate place to donate**

My friend Zinhle set up a BackaBuddy page for me. Please use this link and only this link:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is R25 000 and it's at R11 400 this morning. I'm aware of every single rand of that, and I'm grateful in a way I don't have words for. Zinhle told me to stop feeling weird about it and just accept it, so I'm accepting it. Thank you, Zinhle. And thank you to everyone who has already given.

**PLEASE DO NOT SEND MONEY TO THE "THANDI FIRE RELIEF" PAGE**

There is a fake page called **"Thandi Fire Relief"** on a fundraising website, and there is a WhatsApp message going around asking people to do an EFT to a Capitec account. **That is not me. I have never set up a Capitec account for this and I never will.** I've reported the page and the WhatsApp forward to the platform and to our local police.

If a message asks you to EFT money to a Capitec account because of the fire at Lindale Court, please don't. If it asks you to send to any page other than the BackaBuddy link above, please don't. And please spread this warning on — people are getting taken advantage of, and I'd rather lose nothing than have one more person in this neighbourhood get scammed out of their money. If you want to help and you're not sure, message me and I'll tell you straight.

**What I actually need**

- **Help with a deposit for a new place.** This is the big one. If anyone knows of a rental that a teacher could take on, or if your landlord has a flat going spare, or if you can put in a word with yours, that would mean the world to me. Even knowing something is useful.
- **A laptop.** Mine is gone and all my lesson planning was on it. If you have an old one that still works — it does not need to be pretty or fast, it just needs to open — I will be so grateful. An old tablet with a keyboard would also do.
- **School shoes and work clothes, size 6 (shoes) and size 34 (clothes).** New, or gently used, doesn't matter. If the shoe shop does a trade-in or a discount for teachers, I won't cry, but I'll definitely use it.

That's the list. Genuinely three things.

**What I do NOT need**

- **Clothes.** Please. I have more clothes than I need already — thanks to whoever dropped a bag on my sister's gate at 7am on Sunday morning without knocking, which I love and will return, but no more. I'll pass the extras round to the other flats at Lindale Court.
- **Food.** My sister's freezer is full and her table is a runway. Please don't bring food. If you want to do something, put it towards the deposit and that's it.

And please don't come to my sister's house unannounced with a plate of soup. She's lovely but she has a gate, and I'd rather she didn't become a takeaway.

**For the parents at Little Acorns**

A few things so you're not left guessing:

- **The concert on 27 November is still happening.** Ladybirds will have crowns. I will be buying new ones to laminate, and if anyone has a laminator and some A3 paper I would love to borrow it, but the concert is on.
- **I'm back at school on Wednesday.** I'm going to be there, I'm going to be fine, and I'd really like it to be normal.
- **Please don't make a big thing of it in front of the children.** No candles, no cards, no "is Thandi okay?" in front of the Ladybirds. They don't need to know about ceilings and smoke. They need me to be boring and normal, and that is what I'm going to be. If you want to check on me, check on me quietly afterwards.
- If you have a spare pair of small shoes at home in a size 6, that's a real help for me this week.

**About my replies**

I'm going to be slow. I'm going to be slow for a while. If I don't reply to a DM, it's not that I didn't read it or that I'm ignoring you — there are a lot of you and one very tired teacher with one functioning phone battery. I'm answering comments as I go, in between everything else. Please don't be offended if I don't get to yours first, or at all this week. I promise I'll get there.

**Last thing**

I have never felt so loved by a street. Uncle Faizel in his slippers. Zinhle arguing with me until I accepted help. The mom who left a bag on the gate and ran. My sister's house being full of people. Strangers forwarding this letter to strangers. Someone somewhere already trying to find a flat for me.

I'm overwhelmed and I'm lucky and I know it can't rain on both of us.

Thank you. All of you. For everything.

With so much love and a lot of gratitude,

**Thandi**
(Flat 12, Lindale Court — for those who need to know where to send the laptop, message me and we'll sort it out)
